en: Points of Controversy Great Fifty-Section Third Chapter
The Discussion on the Base of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception: Regarding the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception,
should it not be said that "perception exists"?
“Yes,” you say.

“Is it not the case that non-percipient existence, the non-percipient realm, the abode of non-percipient beings, the cycle of non-percipient saṃsāra, the womb of non-percipient birth, and the acquisition of a non-percipient selfhood must be affirmed?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] … No, indeed.

Is it not the case that existence is perception, destiny is perception, the abode of beings is perception, the round of rebirth is perception, the womb is perception, and the acquisition of individuality is perception?
Yes, it is.
If indeed existence is perception, destiny is perception ... [and so on].
There is the attainment of the state of perception; indeed,
it should not be said that "perception exists" in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
In the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception,
should it not be said that "perception exists"? Yes.
Is "one-facultied existence" (ekavokārabhava) [the same as] a destiny (gati) …pe… the acquisition of a personal identity (attabhāvapaṭilābha)?
It should not be said so …pe….
Is it not the case that existence consisting of four aggregates is a destination … pe … and the acquisition of a personal identity?
Yes, it is.
If four-aggregate existence is a destination … [and so on] … an acquisition of a personal identity, then indeed,
it should not be said that in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception it is not so.
“‘Perception exists. Is it not the case that regarding non-percipient beings, one cannot say “perception exists,” yet that state of non-perception is a destination for non-percipient beings,
an abode for non-percipient beings, a cycle of existence for non-percipient beings, a womb for non-percipient beings, and the acquisition of an individual existence as a non-percipient being?
“Yes,” [he] said.
“In the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, should it not be said that ‘perception exists’?

And yet, is that not a state of non-perception, a destiny of non-perception, an abode of non-perceptual beings, a cycle of non-perception, a womb of non-perception, and the acquisition of a selfhood of non-perception?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Regarding non-percipient beings,
it should not be said that “perception exists,” and yet that is a single-aggregate existence and a destination … [as before] …
Is it the acquisition of a personal existence? Yes.
In the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, it should not be said—
“Perception exists,” yet that is a single-aggregate existence, a destination, a sphere of beings, saṃsāra, a womb, and the acquisition of a personal identity—
is this not so? One should certainly not say so… [and so on]… In the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, one should not say:
“Perception exists,” and that state of perception, that destiny of perception … [and so on] … that acquisition of the individuality of perception? Yes.
Regarding non-percipient beings, one should not say:
"perception exists," nor that it is "existence with perception," "a destination with perception," and so forth,
up to "the acquisition of the individuality of perception"?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … regarding the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception,
it should not be said that "perception exists," and yet that is a four-aggregate existence and a destination … [as before].
Is it the acquisition of a personal existence?
Yes. [Then] regarding non-percipient beings, it should not be said: [that they have acquired a personal existence].
“Perception exists,” and that is the four-aggregate existence, the destiny …pe… the acquisition of a personal identity?
One should not say this …pe….
In the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, should it not be said that "perception exists"?
Yes, it should.
Is it not the case that the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is fourfold existence?
Yes, it is.
If the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is fourfold existence, then indeed you should not say—
“In the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, it should not be said that ‘perception exists.
The fourfold existence consisting of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception should not be said [to exist] in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.”
“Perception exists”? Yes.
Then, should it not be said that the base of infinite space and the fourfold existence in the base of infinite space [exist]? No, they should not be so stated.
“‘Perception exists’?
One should not say so… [and so on]… The base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is fourfold existence; regarding the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, it should not be said that—
“Is there perception?
— Yes.
[And so on for] the base of infinite consciousness …pe…
The base of nothingness is existence consisting of four aggregates; should it not be said of the base of nothingness that "perception exists"?
Indeed, one should not say so… [and so forth].
The base of infinite space is existence consisting of four aggregates; is there perception there? Yes.
The base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is existence consisting of four aggregates; is there perception there?
It should not be said so ... [as before] ...
Is the base of infinite consciousness ...
and the base of nothingness fourfold existence? Is there perception there?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception fourfold existence? Is there perception there?
You should not say so… [as before]… No, indeed.
In the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception,
should it not be said that "perception exists" or "it does not exist"?
Yes, it should.
Is not the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception the fourfold existence? Yes.
If the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is the fourfold existence, then indeed you should not say—
“In the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, it should not be said that ‘perception exists’ or that ‘it does not exist.

The base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is existence in the fourfold plane; in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, it should not be said [that perception exists or does not exist].
“Is there perception, or is there not?”— “Yes.
[The same applies to] the base of infinite space …pe… [and so on].
The base of infinite consciousness …pe… the base of nothingness is fourfold existence. Regarding the base of nothingness,
should it be said that "perception exists" or that "it does not exist"?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is the base of infinite space fourfold existence? Yes. Is there perception there? Yes.
The base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is existence consisting of four aggregates; is there perception there?
You should not say so...
[and so on] ...the base of infinite consciousness... [and so on].
The base of nothingness is existence in the fourfold plane; is there perception there? Yes.
The base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is existence in the fourfold plane; is there perception there?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … In the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception,
should it be said that “perception exists” or that “it does not exist”?
“Yes.
“Is it not the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception?
“Yes.”
If it is the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, then indeed, sir,
you must say: "Regarding the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception,
one should not say either 'perception exists' or 'perception does not exist.'"

Having established [the sphere] as the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, is it not to be said regarding the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception that "perception exists" or "it does not exist"?
Yes, it is so.
Having established that "neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling" is indeed a feeling, should it not be said of neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling that it is either "feeling" or "not-feeling"?
It should certainly not be so stated... [and so on].
The Discussion on the Base of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception is finished.
This is the third chapter.
Its summary verse:
The noble power is common [to all];
the mind with lust is liberated;
that which is liberated is being liberated.
There is the mind being liberated.
For the person who is an eighth-rank practitioner,
the obsession of views has been abandoned.
For the person who is at the eighth stage,
there is no eye among the five faculties;
nor is there the ear established in the Dhamma.
Knowledge of beings according to their deeds;
restraint among the devas;
non-perception among the non-percipient beings—just so it is up to the peak of existence.
